task.situation: Your school’s English blog is running a series called ‘Many languages, one class’. Students have been asked to write about what it’s like to grow up in a class or a neighbourhood where people speak many languages and come from different cultures. The class writes the post for an invented blogger.
task.instruction: Write a blog post. In your blog post you should:
points: describe what makes the blogger’s class or neighbourhood multicultural
explain the advantages and the challenges of growing up in a multicultural environment
suggest how young people from different backgrounds can learn from each other

words.short: Give your blog post a title. Write around 250 words.
words.long: Give your blog post a title. Write around 350 words.

task.de: Blogbeitrag für den Englisch-Blog der Schule (Titel, Username, Datum und Uhrzeit, lockerer und persönlicher Ton, Kurzformen erlaubt, Leser:innen ansprechen, zum Kommentieren einladen). Drei Inhaltspunkte: beschreiben, was die Klasse oder Wohngegend der erfundenen Bloggerin bzw. des erfundenen Bloggers multikulturell macht; Vorteile UND Herausforderungen erklären; vorschlagen, wie Jugendliche voneinander lernen können. Positiv, respektvoll, ohne Klischees. Den Titel wählen wir zum Schluss.

focus.label: informal phrases
focus.note: Marked: informal, conversational phrases typical of blogs (Hi everyone, pretty, loads of, Trust me …). Contractions are allowed but not marked.

gaps.q: How many languages might a class of 26 students speak at home? Shout a realistic estimate.
gaps.qDe: Wie viele Sprachen könnten in einer Klasse mit 26 Schüler:innen zu Hause gesprochen werden? Schätzt eine realistische Zahl. Niemand muss etwas über sich verraten.

gaps.q: Our blogger’s best friend needs a first name. What is it?
gaps.qDe: Ruft einen Vornamen für die beste Freundin oder den besten Freund. Keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen.

steps.q: How do we open our blog post?
steps.de: Der erste Absatz führt die Leser:innen zum Thema unseres Blogbeitrags. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then finish the introduction in your own words: talk to your readers and make them curious.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann den Einstieg mit eigenen Worten fertigschreiben: Leser:innen ansprechen, neugierig machen.

options.label: Greet readers and ask a question
options.text: {{[[Hi everyone!]] How many languages can you hear}} on the tram to school? This morning, I counted six, and I’m [[pretty]] sure I missed a few. {{That’s what I love about}} my city: the whole world is right on my doorstep.
options.why: A greeting and a question speak to readers directly, like in a conversation.

options.label: Start with a scene
options.text: {{Imagine our school corridor at break time.}} Two friends are chatting in a mix of Polish and German, a group is laughing at a joke in Turkish, and somebody is practising a K-pop dance. {{[[Sounds like chaos?]] For us, it’s just}} a normal Tuesday.
options.why: A lively scene puts readers right into our school and shows the topic instead of naming it.

options.label: Start with the main point
options.text: The biggest advantage of a multicultural class is that you learn something new every day. You learn words in other languages, and you try food from all over the world. There are some problems, too, but more about that later. Hi everyone, and welcome to my blog!
options.reject: The order is upside down: the advantages belong in a later paragraph, and the greeting comes last. An introduction greets readers first and leads them to the topic with a hook.
options.rejectDe: Falsche Reihenfolge: Die Begrüßung gehört an den Anfang, die Vorteile kommen erst in einem späteren Absatz.

steps.q: Content point 1: what makes our environment multicultural?
steps.de: Erster Inhaltspunkt: was unsere Klasse oder unsere Wohngegend multikulturell macht. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then describe the blogger’s class or neighbourhood with two details. You can invent them.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Klasse oder Wohngegend aus dem Blog mit zwei Details beschreiben. Die Details dürfen erfunden sein.

options.label: Our class
options.text: {{In my class, there are}} 26 of us, {{and together our families speak}} {N} different languages. Our class group chat is full of words that no translation app understands, and on birthdays we sing ‘Happy Birthday’ in several languages. {{[[No joke!]] It’s like a mini United Nations,}} just with more homework.
options.why: Concrete details and a funny comparison make the class come alive.
options.textLong: {{In my class, there are}} 26 of us, {{and together our families speak}} {N} different languages. Our class group chat is full of words that no translation app understands, and on birthdays we sing ‘Happy Birthday’ in several languages. {{My best friend}} {FRIEND} {{speaks three languages}} and switches between them faster than I can unlock my phone. {{I’ve picked up [[a whole bunch of]]}} new words from {FRIEND}, and in return I’ve taught my friend a few words of my grandparents’ dialect. {{[[No joke!]] It’s like a mini United Nations,}} just with more homework.

options.label: Our neighbourhood
options.text: {{You can see the same mix in my neighbourhood.}} Every morning, I walk past bakeries and restaurants from all over the world, and the shop signs use at least three different alphabets. {{At our weekly market,}} you can buy food from ten countries. {{[[Basically,]]}} it’s a trip around the world without a plane ticket.
options.why: A walk through the neighbourhood gives readers pictures they can see, smell and taste.
options.textLong: {{You can see the same mix in my neighbourhood.}} Every morning, I walk past bakeries and restaurants from all over the world, and the shop signs use at least three different alphabets. {{At our weekly market,}} you can buy food from ten countries. {{A few weeks ago, my best friend}} {FRIEND} {{invited me to}} a big family party round the corner. I didn’t know the dances, but my friend’s cousins showed me the steps, and soon I was dancing [[like a pro]]. {{[[Well, sort of]].}} {{[[Basically,]]}} living here is a trip around the world without a plane ticket.

options.label: Class and neighbourhood
options.text: In my class, there are 26 of us, and together our families speak {N} different languages. However, our class group chat is full of words that no translation app understands. My neighbourhood is just as international, with restaurants and shops from all over the world. Instead, it’s a trip around the world without a plane ticket.
options.reject: The linking words don’t fit: a chat full of other languages is a result of all the languages at home, not a contrast (‘However’ → So), and ‘Instead’ replaces nothing: the last sentence sums up the neighbourhood (→ Basically).
options.rejectDe: Die Linking words passen nicht: However (Gegensatz) steht vor einer Folge, und Instead ersetzt nichts, der letzte Satz fasst nur zusammen.
options.textLong: In my class, there are 26 of us, and together our families speak {N} different languages. However, our class group chat is full of words that no translation app understands. My best friend {FRIEND} speaks three languages and switches between them faster than I can unlock my phone. My neighbourhood is just as international, with bakeries and restaurants from all over the world and a weekly market with food from ten countries. Instead, it’s a trip around the world without a plane ticket, and I love every minute of it.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then describe the blogger’s class or neighbourhood with two details and add something about the blogger’s best friend. You can invent the details.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Klasse oder Wohngegend aus dem Blog mit zwei Details beschreiben und etwas über die beste Freundin oder den besten Freund ergänzen. Details dürfen erfunden sein.

steps.q: Content point 2: what are the advantages and the challenges?
steps.de: Zweiter Inhaltspunkt: Vorteile und Herausforderungen in einem Absatz. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then explain one advantage and one challenge in your own words. Stay fair and respectful.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann einen Vorteil und eine Herausforderung mit eigenen Worten erklären. Fair und respektvoll bleiben.

options.label: What I get out of it, and what is hard
options.text: Living in such a mixed class has big advantages, but it has its challenges as well. You learn very much about other cultures, and since I am in this class, I can say ‘thank you’ in ten languages. I also become invited to lots of birthday parties with delicious food from all over the world. The hardest part is for newcomers: if they don’t speak much German yet, lessons are hard to follow, and that can be really frustrating at first.
options.reject: Three typical mistakes: ‘learn very much’ (→ learn a lot), ‘since I am in this class’ (→ since I have been in this class) and ‘I become invited’ (→ I get invited).
options.rejectDe: Drei typische Fehler: learn very much → learn a lot, since I am → since I have been, become invited → get invited (eingeladen werden = get invited, nicht become).
options.textLong: Living in such a mixed class has big advantages, but it has its challenges as well. You learn very much about other cultures, and since I am in this class, I can say ‘thank you’ in ten languages. I also become invited to lots of birthday parties with delicious food from all over the world. The hardest part is for newcomers: if they don’t speak much German yet, lessons are hard to follow, and that can be really frustrating at first. At break time, small groups sometimes form around one language, so others can feel left out.

options.label: New eyes, and some misunderstandings
options.text: {{My favourite part of living like this, and sometimes the trickiest, is that}} you learn to see the world through other people’s eyes. What’s ‘normal’ for me is [[totally]] new for someone else, and the other way round. {{As a result, you stop thinking}} there’s only one ‘right’ way to live. {{Of course, it’s not always easy.}} A joke that’s funny in one language can sound rude in another. {{[[The good news?]]}} We usually end up laughing about it.
options.why: Explains a deeper advantage, then turns fairly to a challenge. ‘As a result’ shows the effect.
options.textLong: {{My favourite part of living like this, and sometimes the trickiest, is that}} you learn to see the world through other people’s eyes. What’s ‘normal’ for me is [[totally]] new for someone else, and the other way round. Some of my classmates celebrate New Year twice, for example. {{As a result, you stop thinking}} there’s only one ‘right’ way to live. {{Of course, it’s not always easy.}} A joke that’s funny in one language can sound rude in another, and people have different ideas about what’s polite. {{[[The good news?]]}} We usually end up laughing about our mistakes.

options.label: Languages and friends, but a tough start
options.text: {{Growing up like this has [[loads of]] advantages and a few challenges.}} You pick up words in languages you’ve never studied, and you discover music and films you’d never find on your own. {{[[On top of that,]] you make friends with people who}} see things differently. {{For newcomers, though, the start can be tough.}} If you don’t speak much German yet, it’s hard to follow lessons, and it can take months to find your feet.
options.why: Names concrete advantages first, then one honest challenge, so the paragraph stays fair.
options.textLong: {{Growing up like this has [[loads of]] advantages and a few challenges.}} You pick up words in languages you’ve never studied, and you discover music and films you’d never find on your own. {{[[On top of that,]] you make friends with people who}} see things differently. {{For newcomers, though, the start can be tough.}} If you don’t speak much German yet, it’s hard to follow lessons, and it can take months to find your feet. {{[[And let’s be honest,]]}} groups sometimes form around one language, which can make others feel left out.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then explain the advantages and the challenges in your own words and give an example. Stay fair and respectful.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann Vorteile und Herausforderungen mit eigenen Worten erklären und ein Beispiel geben. Fair und respektvoll bleiben.

steps.q: Content point 3: how can young people learn from each other?
steps.de: Dritter Inhaltspunkt: unsere Vorschläge für Jugendliche mit verschiedenen Hintergründen. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add your own ideas and explain why they work.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann eigene Ideen ergänzen und begründen.

options.label: Easy ideas for every class
options.text: {{Luckily, there are [[lots of]] ways to learn from each other.}} {{[[For starters,]]}} why not swap ten words a week with a tandem partner? {{Another idea is}} a monthly ‘culture corner’ where everyone can bring a song or a recipe from home. {{[[Trust me,]]}} people love sharing what matters to them.
options.why: Concrete, easy ideas that any class can try tomorrow.
options.textLong: {{Luckily, there are [[lots of]] ways to learn from each other.}} {{[[For starters,]]}} why not swap ten words a week with a tandem partner? {{Another idea is}} a monthly ‘culture corner’ where everyone can bring a song or a recipe from home. {{Ideas like these help [[the new kid]] most.}} When my family moved from a village in Tyrol to the city, nobody understood my dialect, and it took me [[ages]] to feel at home. {{[[Trust me,]]}} people love sharing what matters to them, and nobody stays [[the new kid]] for long.

options.label: Clear recommendations
options.text: It is strongly recommended that young people from different cultural backgrounds participate in organised exchange activities, such as language tandems. Furthermore, it is advisable to establish regular intercultural workshops in which participants present the customs of their families. It is essential that all participants demonstrate respect at all times. Such measures will undoubtedly contribute to mutual understanding.
options.reject: Far too formal and stiff for a blog post: ‘It is strongly recommended’, ‘Furthermore’, ‘it is advisable’ and ‘undoubtedly’ sound like an official report. A blog talks to its readers in a friendly, personal way.
options.rejectDe: Viel zu förmlich und steif für einen Blog („It is strongly recommended“, „Furthermore“, „it is advisable“, „undoubtedly“): Das klingt wie ein offizieller Bericht. Ein Blog spricht die Leser:innen freundlich und persönlich an.
options.textLong: It is strongly recommended that young people from different cultural backgrounds participate in organised exchange activities, such as language tandems. Furthermore, it is advisable to establish regular intercultural workshops in which participants present the customs of their families. It is essential that all participants demonstrate respect at all times. In addition, newly arrived pupils should be assigned a peer mentor for their first weeks. It is also advisable to hold an annual cultural festival at which students present the traditions of their families. Such measures will undoubtedly contribute to mutual understanding.

options.label: Do things together
options.text: {{The best way to make all this work is to}} do things together. Why not organise a games afternoon where everyone teaches the others a game from their childhood? {{[[Honestly,]] you learn more about someone}} in one afternoon of games than in a year of sitting next to them.
options.why: Answers the challenges with one clear idea: shared activities connect people.
options.textLong: {{The best way to make all this work is to}} do things together. Why not organise a games afternoon where everyone teaches the others a game from their childhood? {{Just asking someone to join in}} can make a huge difference. When I joined a new volleyball club last year, I felt [[a bit lost]] until a girl from my team taught me a card game from her grandmother’s village in Bosnia. Within a week, we were swapping playlists. {{[[Honestly,]] you learn more about someone}} in one afternoon of games than in a year of sitting next to them.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then add your own ideas, explain why they work and tell how the blogger once felt as the new kid. You can invent the details.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann eigene Ideen ergänzen, begründen und erzählen, wie es der Bloggerin oder dem Blogger einmal als Neue:r ging. Details dürfen erfunden sein.

steps.q: How do we end our blog post?
steps.de: Der letzte Absatz beendet unseren Blogbeitrag. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then finish with your own question or invitation to your readers.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann mit einer eigenen Frage oder Einladung an die Leser:innen enden.

options.label: Ask for comments
options.text: {{All these languages make my life richer, even on the tricky days.}} {{[[So, what about you?]]}} Does your class or your neighbourhood sound similar? {{[[Drop me a comment]] below}} and tell me what you’ve learnt from friends with a different background!
options.why: Sums up the post in one sentence, then asks readers for their own stories.

options.label: Give readers a challenge
options.text: {{Living with so many languages isn’t always easy, but it’s a gift.}} {{Here’s my challenge for this week:}} learn to say ‘hello’ and ‘thank you’ in a classmate’s home language. {{[[I bet]]}} they’ll smile. {{Tell me in the comments}} how it went!
options.why: Sums up both sides in one sentence and gives readers a small, friendly task to comment on.

steps.q: Now that the blog post is finished, which title do we choose?
steps.de: Der Titel kommt zuletzt und soll neugierig machen und zum Inhalt passen.
steps.own: Short and catchy: make readers curious about growing up multicultural.
steps.ownDe: Kurz und treffend: Der Titel soll neugierig auf das Thema machen.

options.label: A big picture
options.text: The whole world on my doorstep
options.why: Short and positive, and it sums up the main idea of the post.

options.label: An honest promise
options.text: Growing up multicultural: the good and the tricky
options.why: Tells readers that they will get both sides: advantages and challenges.

options.label: A catchy line
options.text: So many languages, so much to learn
options.why: Short and catchy: it names the topic and promises that there is something to learn.

checks.en: A title that makes readers curious, with user name, date and time under it
A friendly opening that speaks to readers directly
All three content points: description, advantages and challenges, suggestions
Positive and respectful: no stereotypes about any group
Informal, conversational register: contractions are fine, mistakes are not
The post ends with an invitation to comment
Five paragraphs: each body paragraph opens with a clear link to the one before

teacher.aim: Die Klasse baut gemeinsam einen Blogbeitrag (B1) über das Aufwachsen in einer Klasse mit vielen Sprachen und Kulturen und übt dabei Blog-Konventionen und informelle, gesprächsnahe Wendungen, ohne dass der Text fehlerhaft oder respektlos wird. Mehrsprachigkeit erscheint als Stärke.
teacher.prep: A/B/C/D-Karten austeilen, Hefte bereitlegen. Beamer im Vollbild. Im Gerüst-Modus den eingebauten Timer nutzen: 5 min pro Absatz (Body 2: 7 min), bei Bedarf +1. Die Zahl der Familiensprachen wird nur geschätzt, nicht per Handzeichen erhoben. Die Aufgabe am Beamer enthält alles Nötige.
teacher.heft: Neue Seite: Datum rechts oben, darunter „Blog post“ als Überschrift (wie am Beamer). Dann 2 Zeilen für den Titel frei lassen (der Titel kommt zuletzt), darunter Username, Datum und Uhrzeit in einer Zeile (wie am Beamer). Jeder der fünf Absätze beginnt nach einer Leerzeile, am Rand steht das Kurzwort: Intro, Body 1, Body 2, Body 3, Conclusion. Informelle Wendungen grün unterstreichen.
teacher.flow: 6 Entscheidungen: fünf Absätze (jede Entscheidung ist ein ganzer Absatz) und der Titel. Body 2 behandelt Vorteile und Herausforderungen in einem Absatz. Volltext kurz (50 min): 5 min Aufgabe und Kopf, 6 Entscheidungen à ca. 2 min, Abschreiben ca. 20 min, 5 min Checkliste. Volltext lang (Doppelstunde): dieselben 6 Entscheidungen, aber die drei Body paragraphs sind länger, daher ca. 30–35 min Abschreiben; die restliche Zeit für die Besprechung der Fallen und den Beginn der Hausübung nutzen. Gerüst kurz (realistisch ca. 60 min): 5 min Aufgabe und Kopf; pro Absatz 1 min Entscheidung, 5–6 min eigenes Schreiben (Body 2: 7 min, weil Vorteil und Herausforderung hineingehören), 1 min Vergleich mit dem Modell; am Ende 5 min Checkliste. In einer 50-Minuten-Stunde den Schluss noch abstimmen und das Gerüst abschreiben lassen; Schluss fertigschreiben und eigenen Titel finden als Hausübung. Gerüst lang: Doppelstunde (100 min), gleicher Rhythmus, für jeden Body paragraph 7–8 min eigenes Schreiben, dazwischen eine Vergleichsrunde zu zweit.
teacher.traps: Introduction C (CC): falsche Reihenfolge, die Vorteile stehen vor der Begrüßung. Body 1 C (CC): Linking words passen nicht zur Logik (However vor einer Folge, Instead ersetzt nichts). Body 2 A (LSA): learn very much, since I am, become invited. Body 3 B (LSR): viel zu förmlich und steif für einen Blog (It is strongly recommended, Furthermore, it is advisable, undoubtedly), klingt wie ein offizieller Bericht. Kürzel: TA = Erfüllung der Aufgabenstellung, CC = Kohärenz und Kohäsion, LSR = Spektrum sprachlicher Mittel, LSA = Sprachrichtigkeit.
teacher.notes: Der Blogbeitrag hat in beiden Längen genau fünf Absätze (Intro, Body 1 Beschreibung, Body 2 Vorteile und Herausforderungen, Body 3 Vorschläge, Conclusion). Die lange Fassung hat dieselben Entscheidungen; die drei Body paragraphs sind länger, Einleitung und Schluss bleiben gleich. In der langen Fassung kommt in Body 1 die beste Freundin oder der beste Freund dazu, und Body 3 erzählt vom Neu-Sein ohne Migrationsgeschichte (Umzug aus einem Dorf in Tirol oder neu in einem Volleyballverein). Sensibles Thema (Herkunft, Identität): Niemand muss Herkunft, Religion, Aufenthaltsstatus oder die eigenen Familiensprachen offenlegen, keine Einzelperson spricht „für“ eine Gruppe. Die Zahl der Sprachen ist nur eine Schätzung für eine erfundene Klasse mit 26 Schüler:innen. Im Gerüst-Modus dürfen alle Details erfunden sein; niemand schreibt über eigene private Erfahrungen. Für die Namenslücke nur erfundene Vornamen verwenden, keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen. Stadt und Wohngegend bleiben ohne Namen. Mehrsprachigkeit wird als Stärke gezeigt; Klischees über Nationalitäten sofort ansprechen. Falls Erfahrungen mit Ausgrenzung zur Sprache kommen, auf Schulpsychologie oder Rat auf Draht (147) hinweisen. Differenzierung: Schnelle ergänzen im Gerüst-Modus einen eigenen Vorschlag. Hausübung: Blog-Kommentar (ca. 150 Wörter) auf den Blogbeitrag mit einer eigenen Idee, wie Jugendliche voneinander lernen können.
